rules.name: Honors (optional)
rules.desc:
The Honors Degree in Classics is designed for students who demonstrate exceptional academic performance and a commitment to scholarly research within the field. To qualify for this prestigious designation, students must fulfill the following criteria:
GPA Requirement: A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.6 within the major is required to ensure a strong foundation in Classics.
Course Requirement: Upon approval of the final proposal, students may enroll in CLASSICS199
Undergraduate Thesis: Senior Research during their senior year. Participants can earn up to 6 units per term, with a total maximum of 10 units, which may contribute toward fulfilling major requirements. Candidates must complete an honors thesis, which serves as a capstone of their scholarly work.
Supervisor Selection: Students are required to select a tenure-track Classics professor or the Director of Undergraduate Studies to supervise their thesis.
Additional information, including the proposal submission deadlines, can be found on the Classics webpage.

rules.name: Depth Requirement
rules.desc:
Complete anywhere from 20-24 units of ancient history and civilization courses.
Suggested courses can be found below. Additional courses, including Latin, Ancient Greek, and Sanskrit (SNSKTLNG1-3) language courses, and IntroSems courses may count toward this requirement if approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

rules.name: Breadth Requirements
rules.desc:
Complete at least 4 units in the areas “Greek and Roman Archaeology and art” and “Historical and social theory”, and at least 8 units in the area “Comparative ancient civilizations” as described below, so as to reach a total of 16-20 units.
Other courses may count toward this requirement with approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

grading: All courses taken for the major and minor must be completed with a letter grade. Courses receiving a grade lower than a C will not be considered toward fulfilling major or minor requirements.
policies:
Independent Study: Enrollment in the independent study section (CLASSICS198 Directed Readings) requires prior approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies. A maximum of three enrollments, totaling no more than 10 units, may be counted toward the major.
Graduate Courses: Undergraduate students may take 300-level graduate courses with approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies.
Study Abroad Opportunities: If a student wishes to earn credit towards their degree when studying abroad, they are strongly encouraged to meet with the Director of Undergraduate Studies prior to applying. Information about other Classics related travel and research opportunities can be found here.
Subplan Declaration: The BA degree can be earned by fulfilling the requirements for one of the designated subplans. These subplans must be declared in Axess and will be reflected on the student’s transcript, although they will not appear on the diploma.
It is recommended that students regularly consult with the Director of Undergraduate Studies to ensure they are meeting all requirements and to take full advantage of academic opportunities available within the program.
transferPolicy: University credit earned by placement tests or advanced placement work in secondary school is not counted toward any major requirement in the department. Work done at other universities or colleges is subject to department evaluation and the university’s transfer credit process.
reviewNotes: Everyone takes CLASSICS 150, which is both the WIM course and the capstone, and completes one subplan: Classical Studies, Ancient History, Greek, Latin, or Greek and Latin (65 units). Each subplan's listed requirements are checked, and its CLASSICS electives make up the rest of the 60 units. Every course must be letter graded with a C or better, and at most 10 units of CLASSICS 198 directed reading and at most 10 units of CLASSICS 199 honors research count. You check by hand courses the Director of Undergraduate Studies approves (300-level graduate courses, repeated language courses, other courses for the Ancient History requirements), that AP or placement credit is not counted, and for honors CLASSICS 199, the 3.6 GPA in the major and the thesis.
